question: How does Morgan Stanley convert workplace and stock-plan participants into wealth management clients?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 earnings transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes its three channels—financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE—as comprising its "strategic client acquisition model," positioning Workplace as the top of the funnel for acquiring wealth management clients.

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), the CFO described the funnel as beginning with retaining vested workplace assets (which translates into net new assets), followed over time by channel migration where workplace assets seek advice and move into the adviser-led channel.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley describes 'channel migration' as workplace assets that began in the Workplace channel moving into the advisor-led channel, with $300 billion doing so since 2020.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley attributes the migration of workplace-originated assets into the advisor-led channel to its consistent investments in its differentiated platform.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes Workplace as bringing relationships and assets onto the platform, and then delivering advice and solutions to those relationships to build fee-based assets.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes its Morgan Stanley at Work business as positioning it as an early trusted advisor to private companies, where employees benefit from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice as companies grow.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley describes its investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels as driving its 'differentiated client acquisition funnel.'
Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that 70% of the flows originating from workplace are net new assets to the firm.

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Morgan Stanley states that since 2020 it has generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes a referral-based partnership with Carta under which private companies moving from private to public are referred to Morgan Stanley, supporting conversion into its platform.

Morgan Stanley: The strategic-update deck (published January 15, 2026) depicts a client lifecycle in which workplace founders and employees move from financial wellness and equity compensation through to full-service wealth advice and asset allocation as companies go public.

Morgan Stanley: In its 3Q25 10-Q (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley defines the workplace channel as including equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.

Morgan Stanley: In its 3Q25 10-Q (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley defines stock plan participants as total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel, with individuals holding accounts in multiple plans counted in each plan.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), the CFO described the workplace channel as a powerful asset acquisition tool, with the reopening of the IPO market supporting net new assets.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the CFO said Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform and is a strong contributor to the top of the funnel, with stock plan IPO flows representing just over half of overall net new assets in the quarter.

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the CEO said the financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE channels together comprise the firm's strategic client acquisition model.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year 2025, versus historical averages of around $60 billion per year.

Morgan Stanley: In the first quarter of 2025 (period ended March 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that assets migrating to the advisor-led channel that originated from the workplace channel increased by an incremental $20 billion, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated from workplace since the channel expanded in 2020.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the firm said it has about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in its workplace pipeline, with IPOs serving as a source of net new assets at the top of the funnel.
Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), the CFO said 70% of the flows that originate from the workplace channel are actually net new assets to the firm.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), the CFO said the firm is working on a referral model that can begin as early as the financial education spot to convert workplace clients into advice-based (advisor-led) relationships.

Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), the CEO said the Morgan Stanley at Work business positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies, with employees benefiting from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2025), the CFO said the firm historically had about $16 billion per year originating from workplace, and was running ahead of that in 2025.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), the CFO said workplace has been a contributor to net new assets, fee-based flows, and channel migration, citing a $300 billion workplace migration figure and about $60 billion of migration per year historically.

Morgan Stanley: The strategic update deck (published January 15, 2026) showed advisor-led flows from workplace and E*TRADE of approximately $60 billion average for 2020-2024 and approximately $100 billion for 2025.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the CEO described the attachment points that bring clients to E*TRADE and, where appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to advisers, with clients acquired in the corporate stock plan (workplace) context.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), the CFO said the firm's pipeline and connectivity across channels allows it to build relationships early and deepen them over time.

Morgan Stanley: In its 2Q26 supplement (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley's Workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions (stock plan administration) for companies, their executives and employees, and this channel is the entry point through which workplace/stock-plan participants are engaged.

Morgan Stanley: In its 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management segment provides workplace services, including stock plan administration, and retirement plan services, as one of three channels (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace) through which it supports clients.

Morgan Stanley: In its strategic-update deck (published January 15, 2026), Morgan Stanley offers a client lifecycle offering spanning financial wellness and employee benefits, founders wealth strategies, full-service wealth advice and asset allocation, family office solutions, trust & estate planning, private shares trading & lending, and IPO execution and support services to move participants from workplace/employee stage into full wealth relationships.

Morgan Stanley: In its strategic-update deck (published January 15, 2026), Morgan Stanley's 'MS at Work' offering provides stock plan and 401(k) administration, cap table management, cash management solutions, and private capital markets/tender/financing and IPO services for late-stage/IPO companies.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes using referral models and technology such as the 'LeadIQ' product to match individuals (including workplace participants) with advisers, with the goal of becoming their principal financial adviser.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley describes an exclusive partnership with Carta through which private stock plan/corporate companies are referred to Morgan Stanley as they go public, providing a seamless experience to convert those participants into wealth clients.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes offering advice-based services to founders and individuals of private companies through its Carta relationship, deepening relationships as companies transition from private to public.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes its referral model for workplace participants as beginning as early as the financial education spot and with 401(k) assets, to help individuals understand where they could use advice.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states it continues to expand its retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants, creating opportunities to build advice-based relationships over time.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley describes providing financial wellness programs to company employees as part of the Integrated Firm, spanning from advice in corporate boardrooms to financial wellness programs for that company's employees.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes an AI-powered lead distribution platform called LeadIQ that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes, for workplace participants who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, a referral model that can begin as early as the financial education spot and also through 401(k) assets.

Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes driving channel migration from workplace to advisor-led through technology and investment, as workplace assets begin seeking advice.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that assets that originate from workplace migrate into the advisor-led channel as a result of consistent investments into its differentiated platform.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley at Work, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions Morgan Stanley as an early trusted advisor to private companies, and employees benefit from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley describes beginning at the top of the funnel with corporate coverage, using the Integrated Firm to build corporate relationships that lead to workplace relationships.

Morgan Stanley: In its 1Q25 transcript (period ended March 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley describes advisors engaging retail clients by sending 'next best actions,' and the firm has seen increased responses to these engagements.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley states that since 2020 (over roughly the last five years), it has seen $300 billion of assets initiate in the Workplace channel and move into the advisor-led channel.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states it has seen about $60 billion of workplace-to-advisor-led migration per year, and as of the third quarter of 2025 was exceeding that pace on a full-year basis.

Morgan Stanley: In its strategic-update deck (published January 15, 2026), Morgan Stanley defines 'Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE' as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley reports LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors, as one of its early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot. Why it might matter: the CFO said the firm is working on a referral model that can begin as early as the financial education spot to convert workplace clients into advice-based (advisor-led) relationships.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley reports a recently announced partnership with Carta that puts the firm at the center of new client stock plan opportunities as private companies consider going public. Why it might matter: the source states this positions the firm to be referred private companies by Carta as they move into going public, providing a seamless experience for those clients.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley reports deepening its competitive moats through an expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and announced partnerships with Zero Hash in digital assets. Why it might matter: the source states these investments reinforce its leadership in the industry and enhance its ability to service its clients with unique capabilities.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley reports that its Morgan Stanley at Work business, through its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions the firm as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies, enabling workplace employees to benefit from equity compensation plan management, liquidity opportunities and full-service advice as workplace companies grow. Why it might matter: the source states this capability supports clients throughout an entire life cycle, from the firm being an early trusted advisor as workplace companies grow.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states it is now in a singular position in the industry because of the integrated scaling of its client acquisition funnel, including a differentiated workplace offering that continues to expand and source new relationships.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q25 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that its investments in the workplace channel, including its collaboration with Carta and partnerships with Zero Hash, deepen its competitive moats and reinforce its leadership in the industry.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q25 transcript (period ended December 31, 2025), Morgan Stanley states that both net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion for the full year demonstrate industry-leading growth.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states it remains the industry leader with record net new assets of $148 billion and strong fee-based flows of $39 billion, underpinned by its client acquisition funnel.
Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states it has about 70% of the top 100 unicorns by market cap in terms of its workplace pipeline.

Morgan Stanley: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states that since acquiring E*TRADE and expanding its workplace offering, it has added over $2 trillion of net new assets, demonstrating a differentiated client acquisition funnel and a powerful competitive advantage.

Morgan Stanley: In its 4Q24 transcript (period ended December 31, 2024), Morgan Stanley states that its investments in self-directed and Workplace channels drive its differentiated client acquisition funnel.

Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), Morgan Stanley states that the workplace channel brings relationships and assets onto the platform and that these capabilities set the firm apart.

Morgan Stanley: A comparison versus competitors or the industry cannot be made on this evidence as a same-basis ranking, because Morgan Stanley's positioning statements are its own qualitative claims (self-described industry leadership, competitive moats, and differentiated funnel) rather than a common metric compared across firms; the underlying conversion figures are marked unverified and are never compared across firms. The positioning rests on self-reported net new assets and funnel statements: industry-leading growth described via net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion for FY2025, record net new assets of $148 billion for 2Q26, about 70% of the top 100 unicorns in its workplace pipeline, and over $2 trillion of net new assets since acquiring E*TRADE and expanding its workplace offering.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley does not report a conversion rate, penetration figure, or count of workplace/stock-plan participants converted into wealth management clients; the firm reports related quantities (asset migration amounts, advisor-led flows, total stock plan participants, and net new assets) but no figure defined as participant conversion.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Q/K disclosures and earnings transcripts for any metric specifically defined as participant conversion.
